title: NaN equals NaN in `=`, grouping, `DISTINCT` and joins
description: Spark documents `NaN = NaN` as true; NaN values group together and match in join keys. NaNs with the sign bit set group, deduplicate and join with NaN too: the optimizer's `NormalizeFloatingNumbers` replaces every NaN (and -0.0) in grouping, join and window keys by the canonical NaN (and 0.0). `count(DISTINCT x)` over NaN, -NaN, 0.0, -0.0 is 2.
Arrays compare their elements the same way: `array(NaN) = array(NaN)` is true.
reference: `NAN_IS_NAN` (#89, an override of IEEE equality) for `=`, grouping, `DISTINCT` and joins. Spark is native.

evidence.note: NaN Semantics: NaN = NaN, grouped together, normal in join keys, last in ascending order
NaN and -0.0 are normalised in grouping, join and window keys

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `GROUP BY` over two `double('NaN')` rows gives one group, NaN with count 2
`array_distinct(array(0.0, -0.0, -0.0, NaN, NaN))` is [0.0,NaN]: the NaNs deduplicate (the `-0.0` literals are decimals, already 0.0)
`map_zip_with` of `map(float('NaN'), 1)` and `map(float('NaN'), 2)` matches the NaN keys: {NaN:{"v1":1,"v2":2}}

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
